Hi Susan — thanks for the report and the logs, really helpful. I'm opening an internal incident and we've already started triage. Initial snapshot: we're seeing increased 503s on phoenix-3b in us-west-2 edge pools correlated with longer kernel queue times on a subset of serving hosts.

Immediate actions we're taking:
- Rerouting a percentage of phoenix-3b traffic to phoenix-3b-fallback (quantized variant) to reduce pressure
- Scaling an extra dedicated pool and flushing prefix caches where safe
- Collecting per-host logs and full request traces (I attached an anonymized log extract)

I'll keep you updated every hour until we reach sustained baseline. If things are critical on your side and you want us to divert more traffic, say the word and we can accelerate.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize recovery.

Best,

Marissa/Hannah/Marcus — forwarding BrightCart's report. Key points from their log: 503s and timeouts clustered between 08:45-09:05 PT; app-level traces show "upstream write timeout" and 503s returned by our serving tier.

What we've observed so far from metrics:
- CPU and GPU utilization normal on most hosts but a subset of hosts (rack 7 in us-west-2) show kernel-queue spikes and token-kv eviction churn
- Autoscaler attempt at 08:52 triggered new instances but they failed health checks for a short window (likely due to cache warm-up and probe timeouts)

Suggested immediate mitigation (please action):
1) Pin BrightCart traffic away from rack 7 hosts via routing rule for the next 45 minutes
2) Increase probe timeout from 2s to 8s during warmup for phoenix-3b; this should avoid transient 503s on instance boot
3) Enable temporary fallback routing to phoenix-3b-fallback with 20% weight
4) Post a short customer-facing blurb (I can send) and a recovery ETA once stable

I've attached the runbook reference — please confirm when routing change and probes are applied.

—Dylan

Subject: Update: phoenix-3b incident resolved — follow-up and next steps

Hi Susan — quick update now that we've reached steady state. Summary:

What happened:
- Between 08:45–09:10 PT a subset of us-west-2 serving hosts experienced elevated kernel queue latency combined with aggressive KV cache churn during autoscaler-driven bootstrapping. The combination briefly caused health-check probe failures and increased 503s/timeouts for model variant phoenix-3b.

What we did to mitigate:
- Immediately pinned BrightCart's routes away from the impacted hosts and shifted 30% of traffic to phoenix-3b-fallback (quantized variant) to reduce pressure
- Adjusted probe timeouts during warmup and delayed autoscaler termination to allow cache warming
- Deployed a targeted runtime configuration fix to reduce KV eviction aggressiveness (hotfix v2.1.8) to the affected pool

Status now:
- Error rate for BrightCart has returned to baseline (~0.3% failures, consistent with expected transient network issues); we have not observed further 503 spikes during the afternoon load tests

Next steps / follow-up:
- We're running a full postmortem and will share it by EOD tomorrow with root cause details and longer-term remediation (scheduler heuristics change + probe tuning).
- We'll offer BrightCart a test window to perform integration testing with phoenix-3b-fallback and a plan to gradually migrate back to the main phoenix-3b when we complete the scheduler changes.
- If you want, we can provide an SLA credit review per the contract; happy to coordinate with your procurement team.

Appreciate your patience — we're treating this as a priority. If you'd like a short call to walk through the timeline and mitigations, I can make time tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
